item.title: A Sociolinguistic Analysis of Cloth Names in Ewe
item.description: The main aim of this paper is to explore the sociolinguistic significance of cloth names among the Ewe people. Additionally, the study investigates whether the use of cloth names as communicative modes is still a vital linguistic form in this group. The study utilized a sequential mixed-methods design. item.title: Authentic Consent and the Decolonial Trouble of “Studying Up”
item.description: Studying gender in African Union and national politics, I came across a scenario in which my interview requests were ignored until someone from the donor community vouched for me. item.title: Negotiating Consent in African Studies
item.description: Informed consent has been increasingly equated with standardized models and legal jargon. At Scandinavian universities, researchers are expected to adhere to European standardized models and institutional forms, necessitating documentable (preferably signed) consent from research participants. item.title: Silozi Phrasal Tonology
item.description: In Silozi, High tones are subject to a number of different processes including shift, doubling and deletion. After establishing these on the basis of isolation forms and two-word phrases, this paper examines a range of complex phrases which reveals a very productive process of phrasal High insertion, whereby a High tone is inserted and linked to the final tone bearing unit of any phonological phrase which is not pre-pausal. item.title: Warriors and Colonizers
item.description: This study critically examines (post)colonial ideologies within the Nollywood epic Jagun Jagun (2023), directed by Adebayo Tijjani and Tope Adebayo and produced by Femi Adebayo. Through a colonial reading, the film emerges as a narrative that critiques systems of power, exposes the enduring legacies of colonialism, and accentuates the urgency of African self-determination and youth empowerment. item.title: Trapped in Coloniality
item.description: This article explores how the popular Icelandic Nordic Noir series, Trapped Season 2, provides a nuanced perspective on the deeply rooted concepts of Icelandic and Nordic exceptionalism and homonationalism in popular culture. item.title: From a Kingdom to a Commonwealth
item.description: This article examines the historical trajectory of Denkyira, a once-dominant Akan kingdom in Ghana. It challenges the prevailing narrative that the legacy of Denkyira ended with its defeat by Asante in 1701. Despite its significance as a precolonial West African powerhouse, the Denkyira kingdom remains largely absent from mainstream historical discourse. item.title: Pitch Reset in Akan Subordinate Clauses
item.description: This study explores how lexical tone interacts with intonation in Akan, focusing on pitch reset as a prosodic cue in complex declaratives. Pitch reset – an upward shift in fundamental frequency (f0) following declination – has been documented in various African languages, and in Akan by Kügler (2016, 2017).
